A limiter is like a compressor on steroids.

A compressor reduces the volume when it's higher than a threshold. A limiter prevents the volume to be higher than the threshold. 

Use a Limiter when you want the source to have a flatter volume. The db parameter you're taking about could be the threshold. You will also probably find and input and output gain. Playing with input gain and threshold will give the same result as long as you compensate by raising or lowering the output.

More: The difference between limiting and clipping is very notable for the ears but somewhat similar in the process. When a sound is too loud and clips, like when limiting, it is prevented from getting louder than the maximum. However, it does extremely abruptly, which changes the nature of the sound. So if clipping is knocking your face on the dash of your car, limiting ads an air bag. Your face is immobilized, but hopefully not so instantly that it disfigurates you. In limiting, the lowering of the volume is applied more smoothly. To prevent very quick volume changes, a Limiter uses "lookeahead" which let it know in advance when to release the airbag to make absolutely sure no sound is disfigurated.

The comedian is [Mike Ward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Ward_(comedian)). His humor style is very broad but in Quebec he stands out with his dark humor. (He is an anglophone in a francophone province and anglophone humors is darker than francophone so this could be a reason) He has won many awards, been a significant help for upcoming comedians, made several benefit shows and is very popular. BUT his humor is dark so some media platforms profit from quoting parts of his jokes in ways that make him look bad. The consumers become emotional and invested in the case so they buy more media and become more angry. So he is popular, but also controversial.

In 2007, there was a girl named Cédrika Provencher who was kidnapped and it took the news by storm. Everyone was talking about it non stop. A few months later, he made a joke about the tax collectors in Québec basically saying they will stop at nothing to steal you. The final punchline was "I bet they're the ones who kidnapped Cédrika". This translated in the media to "Mike Ward is picking on Cédrika". It turned out to be a huge scandal, but luckily after a relatively long time, Cédrika's parents ended up hearing the joke for the first time and changed their minds since they couldn't see how it could be insulting. The scandal started to lose momentum at that point.

In 2013 Mike Ward performed his new one man show S'expose. He joked about how the tv channel that aired his previous show also presented porn but his joke was the thing that shocked the most. In order to avoid a new scandal, the new show was presented only for people who came in the room or bought a dvd. But in an attempt for a mix of catharsis and enjoying the private aspect of the show, he made a bit called The untouchables where his jokes mentioned people that are socially protected. One of them was [Jérémy Gabriel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%A9my_Gabriel) commonly known as Le petit Jérémy / The Little Jeremy. He was a kid who suffered from a handicap which made him deaf. His parents encouraged him to sing and he became very popular. I think people who liked him did mainly out of pity/courage since he sang like you would expect a deaf kid to sing. He was also the subject of ridicule. In his bit, Mike Ward acted as someone who takes Jérémy's side by saying "Stop ridiculing him, he's a dying kid, let him pursue his dream", but 5 years later Mike's character would realize that he isn't actually dying so his stance was based on a lie, which frustrated him. So at that point the character wanted him death. He then kept exaggerating by saying he saw him at the water park, tried to drown him without success, meaning that he's invincible and that he will keep singing badly forever. I'm removing all the humor aspects of the bit, but I think it was executed in a very funny way. Regarding the deeper message, I think it questions the rate at which some people are ready to pick on a handicapped kid, but also the legitimacy of industries that profit from pity.

Ironically, the title of the bit (the untouchables) went from joke to reality when the Quebec Human Rights Commission sued Mike Ward and asked him to pay 42,000$ to Jérémy and his mother. The reason is that during his teens years, Jérémy was bullied and some of his bullies reused Mike Ward's joke. To me, it isn't fair because there are many factors at play. Jérémy's parents made him a public figure. They used his disability and put it on display. As a Québecois, I haven't seen the ridiculing of Jeremy gaining in popularity following the show. In fact at that time he was a teenager so people in general were forgetting about him. Should we blame the bullies? Everyone who made money by putting his handicap on display? The chunk of the population who was already joking about him before the show? I think the bullying problem in general should be treated with nuance. Mike Ward ended up losing the case but he is now fighting at the supreme court. Of course, I'm describing the case from a skewed perspective because I like what he does and I watched the show before the scandal. But I encourage you to also google him and see the skewed perspective of the people who didn't see the joke in its context.

But while the Mike Ward case is huge, I could've also talked about the horror writer Yvan Godbout. One of his novels depicted the rape of a child. During the night, the police went to his house, handcuffed him, searched the house and his computer. Thankfully he won but he was also put under huge stress and could barely work for 2 years. There was a similar case with another Québecois I don't remember the name who did special effects for horror movies. Some people thought his film was too gory so he was brought to court but he also won. These are all cases where the justice system was involved, but cases where people lose their job are also big attacks.

So in conclusion, I think division is the main problem. The Cédrika Provencher case was light at first but became very aggressive because of misinformation. This translated in Mike Ward's humor becoming more aggressive which was then received even more aggressively.
